summary: Keeping, breeding, and selling a roof rat is legal in Ohio. The Dangerous Wild Animals Act (ORC ch. 935, post-Zanesville) lists big cats, bears, primates, large constrictors and the like — no rodents. The roof rat is not native wildlife regulated by ODNR (it's actually named a nuisance pest), no Ohio prohibited/exotic list captures the genus Rattus, and Ohio's commercial breeder/dealer licensing (ORC ch. 956) is dogs-only. The one nuance is interstate IMPORT: Ohio's general animal-import rule likely requires a Certificate of Veterinary Inspection for an incoming pet rat (rodents aren't named in either the domestic or non-domestic import rule), so confirm with the State Veterinarian.

keep.why: R. rattus is not a 'dangerous wild animal' under ORC 935.01 (20 enumerated categories; no rodents), not native wildlife regulated by ODNR (it is named a nuisance pest in OAC 1501:31-15-03), and on no Ohio prohibited/exotic-species list (OAC 1501:31-19-01). No statute restricts private possession.

breed.why: No Ohio statute restricts breeding rodents; commercial breeder/retailer licensing (ORC ch. 956) is limited to dogs. R. rattus is outside ch. 935 and ODNR's regulated-wildlife scope, so breeding is unregulated (local zoning/nuisance aside).

sell_give.why: Ohio's animal sales/dealer licensing (ORC ch. 956) covers only dogs and dog pet-stores; no state license attaches to selling or giving away pet rats, and R. rattus is on no restricted/dangerous list. General humane law (ORC ch. 959) applies to all animals.

transport.why: In-state transport is unregulated. For IMPORT, ODA's general rule (OAC 901:1-17-01) requires a CVI for 'domestic animals' entering Ohio; a captive-bred pet rat plausibly reads as 'domestic,' but rodents aren't named in either the domestic or non-domestic (901:1-17-12) import rule, so confirm the exact paperwork with the State Veterinarian.

restrictions.summary: Importing a pet rat into Ohio likely needs a Certificate of Veterinary Inspection (OAC 901:1-17-01); rodents aren't named, so confirm with the ODA State Veterinarian. No CVI for in-state movement.

restrictions.summary: Never release a roof rat — it's a non-native species (and a declared nuisance in Ohio). Rehome responsibly.
